metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Matches Up Well Against Broncos
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey is in line for a productive Week 4 when he squares off against the Denver Broncos. So far in 2026, Denver has given up the third-most rushing yards, has the highest EPA allowed per run, and has the most missed tackles in the league. The Broncos defense will also be missing linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hamstring). This makes for an inviting matchup for McCaffrey, who owns the league's fifth-best rushing success rate and the highest average rushing yards before contact among starting running backs. As usual, McCaffrey can be expected to be one of quarterback Brock Purdy's favorite targets. And with Mike Evans (ribs) questionable and expected to be a game-time decision on Sunday, McCaffrey could see his receiving work increase. The Broncos gave up six catches for 70 yards to Kyren Williams last week. McCaffrey is projected as the overall RB6 in Week 4.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone Sunday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey ran for 75 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries in the 49ers 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. He also caught 4-of-5 targets for 41 yards receiving.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey took over as the clear lead back on Sunday. He found the end zone in the fourth quarter as the Cardinals were making a comeback. He remains a strong RB1 moving forward.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Records 116 total yards in win
metadata.description: McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 75 yards and a touchdown while bringing in four of five targets for 41 yards in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey's carry total was modest by his standards, but he still outpaced backup Kaelon Black by 11 rushes and four targets while also recording a one-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter. McCaffrey was highly efficient with his rushing opportunities, and he finished second in receptions and third in targets for the 49ers on the afternoon. San Francisco's pass-catching corps suffered further attrition this weekend -- Mike Evans exited the game with a rib/oblique injury, while Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Saturday -- so McCaffrey could continue to see his receiving work creep up in a Week 4 home showdown against the Broncos next Sunday.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Set for Bounce-Back Week vs. Cardinals
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey has the opportunity to bounce back when his team hosts the Arizona Cardinals in Week 3. The star back was part of a large contingent of players who didn't participate in Wednesday's practice but returned on Thursday to prepare for Sunday's divisional matchup. McCaffrey was held to 23 yards on 10 carries in Week 2 but scored two rushing TDs in a convincing 35-13 win against the Miami Dolphins. Arizona has struggled to contain the run early in the 2026 campaign, allowing 243 yards and one touchdown on the ground through two games. CMC should be able to exploit the Cardinals' defense, setting the table for a strong Week 3 across fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey (rest) did not take part in San Francisco's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey was given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day, which is normal for him at the first practice of the week. He should be a full go for Sunday's game and remains a must-start fantasy option in all league formats for as long as he stays healthy and on the field.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone twice in Week 2
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey gained 23 yards on 10 carries and 43 yards on four catches, scoring twice on the ground in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Week 2, but McCaffrey did score a pair of one-yard plunges. As usual, the dual-threat back was also active in the passing game. McCaffrey is up to 29 total touches through two games, averaging 4.6 yards per carry and 7.0 yards per reception. The 49ers appear to be capping the 30-year-old's usage a bit, but he's still a clear RB1, particularly in PPR formats, when healthy.

metadata.title: Kaelon Black Keeps a Useful Role Behind Starting RB
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Kaelon Black remains a strong Week 3 waiver target despite a quieter showing against Miami. Black carried seven times for 25 yards after handling 14 carries for 65 yards in the opener, and he played roughly one-third of the offensive snaps Sunday. Christian McCaffrey remains the clear lead back and handled both goal-line touchdowns, so Black's standalone value is still somewhat dependent on game script. Even so, San Francisco has given the rookie 21 carries through two games, which is enough to make his role worth taking seriously. RotoBaller currently recommends adding Black in 10-team leagues and deeper, viewing him as one of fantasy's better handcuffs with some standalone appeal. He does not need to be forced into lineups every week, but the combination of regular rushing work and the upside he would carry if McCaffrey missed time makes Black a worthwhile waiver add rather than a bench-only lottery ticket.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Scores twice to reach 100 career TDs
metadata.description: McCaffrey rushed 10 times for 23 yards and two touchdowns while catching both of his targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey opened the scoring with a one-yard touchdown run in the first quarter and added another one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. The two-touchdown performance brought McCaffrey's career regular-season touchdown total up to 100. Exactly half of those touchdowns have come with the 49ers, as McCaffrey joins Marshall Faulk and Randy Moss as the only players to score at least 50 touchdowns apiece for multiple teams, per ESPN Insights. McCaffrey should continue to contribute as both a runner and a pass catcher in Week 3 against the Cardinals.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey In Line For RB1 Performance In Favorable Matchup
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey had 68 rushing yards on 10 carries and converted eight targets into five catches for 20 receiving yards in last week's win over the Rams. His modest output in that game resulted from the 49ers' overall dominance and the effectiveness of backup Kaelon Black (groin), who had 14 carries of his own. With San Francisco heavily favored against the Dolphins in Week 2, there will be less of a need for McCaffrey to produce. However, Black was nursing groin tightness in practices this week and is listed as questionable for Sunday. Restrictions on Black may increase McCaffrey's workload, or open the door for backup Jordan James to get involved. Regardless, McCaffrey's status in San Francisco's offense and his effectiveness when on the field keep him in contention for a top-five finish. As in any week when McCaffrey is healthy, he is a must-start.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey (rest) returns to practice Thursday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey (rest) returned to practice for the 49ers as a full participant on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: As expected, McCaffrey returns to being a full participant at practice on Thursday after being given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day. He should be good to go for Week 2 and is primed for a huge workload against the Dolphins, especially now that Kaelon Black (groin) has been added to the injury report for the 49ers.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey (rest) did not take part in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey was a non-participant at San Francisco's practice on Wednesday. The team gave him a routine rest day and he should be back on Thursday, so fantasy managers should have no concerns about him heading into a great Week 2 matchup against the Dolphins.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey Played Through Cramping in Season-Opening Win
metadata.description: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said that running back Christian McCaffrey dealt with some cramps during the season-opening win on Thursday over the division-rival Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, but made it through fine, according to ESPN's Nick Wagoner. McCaffrey did not have a huge Week 1 performance, but he did enough to help the Niners pull off a blowout win over a Rams defense that came into the 2026 season expected to be one of the best units in the league. The 30-year-old had 10 carries for 68 yards and caught five of his eight targets for 20 yards. It was a notable reduction in his workload after finishing as the RB1 in fantasy in 2025 with a career- and league-high 413 touches in 17 regular-season starts. Rookie Kaelon Black actually had four more carries than CMC, who did not do much in training camp due to undisclosed tightness. McCaffrey might not see as hefty a workload in 2026, but if he stays healthy again all year, he still has the potential to be a league-winner in San Fran's offense. He is a must-start for a Week 2 matchup against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Sept. 20.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey racks up 88 scrimmage yards in win
metadata.description: Christian McCaffrey ran 10 times for 68 yards and caught five of eight targets for 20 yards in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: McCaffrey surprisingly had a split backfield with Kaelon Black, at least much more than expected. The veteran tied Black in touches, 15 to 15, but had the edge in opportunities, 18 to 15, thanks to receiving. It will be interesting to see if this is a Week 1 fluke or a recurring theme, as Black was involved throughout the game, not just when the game was well in hand. Still, CMC is a top-tier asset, and while today was fine, bigger days are ahead.

metadata.title: Christian McCaffrey - Efficient with modest workload
metadata.description: McCaffrey rushed 10 times for 68 yards and brought in five of eight targets for 20 yards during the 49ers' 27-7 Week 1 win over the Rams in Melbourne, Australia.
metadata.analysis: Coming off a 2025 regular season where he was able to suit up for all 17 games while handling 413 total touches, McCaffrey saw a notable workload reduction to open the new campaign. Rookie third-round pick Kaelon Black actually outpaced McCaffrey by four carries, but it was the latter who edged out his new backfield mate for the team lead in rushing yards. McCaffrey flashed his trademark explosiveness when carrying the ball and should still helm the ground attack on the majority of weeks, although lopsided game scripts in either direction could lead to head coach Kyle Shanahan taking the opportunity to curtail his star running back's volume. McCaffrey will next take aim at what is expected to be a vulnerable Dolphins defense in a Week 2 matchup on Sunday, Sept. 20.
